result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get Katz centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20522-L20663){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.katz_centrality( alpha=0.1, beta=1.0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Katz centrality](/assets/graphs/katz-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph shaded by Katz centrality with alpha 0.5, which counts incoming walks. D receives walks from A, B and C and scores 0.32, E, fed through D, 0.26, B and C 0.16, and the source A, which nothing reaches, 0.11." width="100%"} Katz centrality measures node influence based on the number of walks of all lengths reaching the node, with walks weighted by `α^length`: `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β` where α is the attenuation factor, `Aᵀ` is the transpose of the adjacency matrix, and `β` is a bias vector (constant for all nodes). For directed graphs, this counts incoming paths, making it suitable for measuring "prestige" or "influence received". Key differences from other centralities: - PageRank: uses teleportation and out-degree normalization - Eigenvector: only considers infinite-length walks (principal eigenvector) - Alpha centrality: uses `A` instead of `Aᵀ` (outgoing vs incoming) - Katz: weights walks by path length, considers all finite walks ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attenuation factor for walk lengths. Must be smaller than the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue (typically < `0.2` for safety). Higher values give more weight to longer paths. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Bias/weight added to each node. Acts as a 'free' centrality that every node gets. Higher values reduce the relative importance of network position. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations for convergence. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance threshold. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`katz_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to normalized Katz centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. Scores sum to `1.0`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Katz centrality (Katz, 1953) generalizes eigenvector centrality by giving every node a baseline contribution and geometrically discounting influence with distance. The closed-form solution is $c = \left((I - \alpha A^\top)^{-1} - I\right)\, \beta \mathbf{1}$ (with $\beta$ allowing per-node bias), which converges only when $\alpha < 1/\lambda_{\max}(A)$; sensible defaults sit around $\alpha \approx 0.1$ and rarely above $0.2$. For directed graphs the transpose matters: high Katz signals prestige (many incoming paths, weighted toward short ones), while for undirected graphs $A^\top = A$ and the metric collapses close to alpha centrality. Setting `beta` non-uniform biases the walk in favor of certain seed nodes, which is the standard trick for personalized ranking. Final scores are normalized to sum to $1$ so they can be compared across graphs of different sizes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} "D" receives incoming edges both directly from "A" and indirectly via "B" and "C", so it accumulates the highest Katz score: ::: {#5c0af5f0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_node("D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("A", "D") ) graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.25107441755258986, 1: 0.22619316896629715, 4: 0.27391992761818584, 2: 0.2488124858629269} ``` ::: ::: A smaller `alpha=` weights short paths much more heavily than long ones; a larger value lets longer paths contribute more: ::: {#9d6b3e64 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="D") ) graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.05) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 0.2502898249160251, 1: 0.23780505930263668, 4: 0.26220980351356976, 2: 0.24969531226776853} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#9e8ef767 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.15) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 0.25223868556215884, 1: 0.2151289429101568, 4: 0.2852340871810041, 2: 0.2473982843466803} ``` ::: :::
